name: Tranylcypromine
metabolism: Absorbed quickly and well after a dose by mouth, with peak blood levels at about 2.5 hours and a time in the body of roughly 2 hours. It is broken down a good deal, including the side chain coming apart and probably some joining to small molecules. What it mainly does is block MAO, both MAO-A and MAO-B, and it blocks them permanently; that wears off slowly, and in clinical terms it is treated as reversed within 14 days. How much comes out in the urine depends on how acid the urine is.
summary: Tranylcypromine is a nonselective, irreversible monoamine oxidase inhibitor used primarily to treat major depressive disorder, including treatment-resistant depression.
